1. Selective server test launch

Covers: the whole Service

The Service is in a selective server test launch, by invitation. It can change, break or be withdrawn. We may remove features and, where we have to, reset beta data, and we will tell you first where we can. Tell us what is wrong: any feedback you send may be used by us freely and without payment.

2. Who can use it

Covers: sign-up for the App and for a workspace

You must be 13 or older. If you are 13 to 17, you can use Oneway with the teen protections the Privacy Policy describes, which are on from the start. We do not ask a parent to agree to these Terms for you. Accounts for people under 18 carry the protections the Privacy Policy describes. Some features carry a higher age: Waypass, and selling or messaging a seller on the Marketplace, are for people 18 and over, and casino offers are for people 21 and over. Where the law sets a higher age for a feature, you must meet it. You may not use the Service if you are barred from receiving it under United States law, including export and sanctions law. If you act for a Center, you confirm you have the authority to.

3. Your account, your workspace profile and your birthday

Covers: Me, Settings, workspace sign-up, the OS

Give accurate information. Keep your password and your two-step codes to yourself and tell us at once if someone else has them. You are responsible for what happens under your account.

You may hold one personal account. You do not need an account to look around, to message or book a Center from its page, or to pay a Center; these Terms apply to you when you do.

Your workspace profile is a work name and title you use at the Centers where you work, kept apart from your personal profile. Use your real working name. The Privacy Policy says who sees it.

Your birthday. Give your real birthday. You can change it once, in Settings. In Texas, and in Tennessee, Mississippi and Georgia for some changes, a person at Oneway reviews the change before it applies, as those states’ laws require.

4. What you post

Covers: Create, Home, Me, comments, stories, a Center’s page

What you post is yours. You give Oneway a worldwide licence, free of charge, to host, store, copy, format and show it, to the people your settings allow, so that we can run the Service. The licence ends when you delete the content or your account, except for copies we are required to keep, backups until they are replaced, and content other people have already received, reposted or quoted.

Posts, profiles and followers are public unless you change your settings. You choose your audience.

You promise that you have the right to post what you post, and that it does not break the law or anyone's rights.

Edited posts show Edited. Once others can see a post, an edit that changes what it is (most of its words, its meaning, its picture, a name or a link, or adding more words than it has, though up to 30 is always fine) is refused: post it as a new post instead. Fixing a typo, a price, the hours or a date, or adding a sentence, is fine. The original is shown only to you, unless you choose Show the original to readers, and then only while its words pass the same automatic moderation a post does.

Deleting a post removes it from view. The Privacy Policy says what we keep.

5. Oneway boosts

Covers: new public posts in Home and For you

Oneway may add boosts to a new public post to help it get seen, spread over one to three days.

A boost comes from Oneway itself, never from a person or from an account made to look like one.

A post’s like count may include Oneway boosts, and the author is told when their post is boosted. The list of who liked a post shows only people.

Boosts, and views that come from them, never count toward advertising reach, Center insights, creator earnings or paid placement.

Posts by people under 18, and posts that are not public, are never boosted.

6. Rules

Covers: everything you do on Oneway; the Community Guidelines say more

Do not use Oneway to:

break the law, or help anyone else break it;

harass, threaten, stalk or target a person, or share someone's private information or location without their consent;

post sexual content involving minors, or anything that exploits or endangers a child;

share an intimate picture of someone without their consent;

post content that promotes violence or terrorism, or threatens to hurt someone;

impersonate a person, a business or an organization, or pretend to be Oneway;

copy another site’s, app’s or brand’s design, layout or words to pass it off as theirs or as your own;

send spam, run scams, or post fake reviews or manufactured engagement;

coordinate false reports to get someone else’s account restricted;

upload malware, or attack the Service or get around its limits, security or sign-in;

scrape the Service, or copy data from it, without our written permission;

use recognition, the guest list, location or Waypass to identify, follow or pursue someone against their wishes;

sell anything the Marketplace does not allow;

resell the Service, or build a competing product from it.

If you find a security problem, tell us at the address below, give us a reasonable time to fix it, and do not read, change or keep other people's data to prove it. We will not take action against good-faith research that follows this. The Security page says how to report one.

Oneway has no tolerance for objectionable content or abusive users. We may remove content, limit features, or suspend or end accounts that break these rules or put people at risk. Where we can, we say why.

7. Reports, moderation and account standing

Covers: Report on any post, comment, person, Center or listing; appeals; automatic checks; Shield

Anyone can report a post, comment, person, Center or listing, including hateful conduct, from the App or the website. People review reports. Automated checks can raise or lower a report's priority but cannot act on it. We tell the person who reported what we decided.

If we act on your content or account, you can appeal at the address below, and someone who did not make the first decision will look again.

Automatic checks. Everything you write is read by an automatic check before it shows. Clear harm (threats, slurs, sexual words beside a child, asking a child to keep secrets or to meet) is refused everywhere, messages included. Words that could be harm may hold a post, so only you see it until you change it or a person reviews it. Cursing at a person is not allowed in public. A message to a Center from someone without an account is not sent if the check finds any flagged word or a link. If we read your words wrong, ask for a review.

Account standing. Each account has one standing: normal, watched, held or locked. Refusals by the check move it (three in an hour put an account under watch), and our team can restrict an account or change its standing, with a reason. A watched account’s unsure words are refused, a held account’s posts wait for a person, and a locked account cannot post or send for a time. During an attack we may switch on stricter rules for a while (Shield), and a Center’s managers can do the same for their own pages.

8. Removing intimate pictures

Covers: the Take It Down request form

If an intimate picture of you was shared on Oneway without your consent, you, or someone acting for you, can ask us to remove it at oneway.center/take-it-down . The request needs your name and a way to reach you, the address of each post that shows it, a statement that you believe in good faith it was shared without consent, and your signature (your name, typed). After you confirm the request from the email we send, a person at Oneway reviews it and takes down what it reports, with every identical copy of the same file, within 48 hours. If you tell us the picture shows someone under 18, the posts you named come down as soon as you confirm, while the person reviews it. The person who posted it is never told who asked, and there is no counter-notice that brings it back.

The law: under the TAKE IT DOWN Act (section 3), a covered platform must, on a valid request, remove the intimate image and make reasonable efforts to remove known identical copies, as soon as possible and no later than 48 hours after the request. In plain words: we take it down fast, and we look for copies.

9. Child safety

Covers: every photo and video upload

Never upload sexual content involving a minor. Matching photos and videos against lists of known child sexual abuse material needs approval from the service that keeps those lists, which Oneway does not have yet, so that check is not running. When it runs, on a match the file is never shown, the account is held at once, the file is kept locked as evidence, and a person at Oneway reports it to the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC).

The law: 18 U.S.C. 2258A requires a provider that learns of apparent child sexual abuse material on its service to report it to NCMEC’s CyberTipline, and to preserve what it reported for one year. In plain words: we report it, we keep the evidence, and we do not warn the uploader.

10. Copyright

Covers: the copyright notice form

If you believe something on Oneway infringes your copyright, send a notice at oneway.center/copyright or to hello@oneway.center , and we answer each one. Include the work, where it is on Oneway, your contact details, a statement that you believe in good faith the use is not allowed, and a statement, under penalty of perjury, that the notice is accurate and that you own or act for the owner. On a valid notice, once you confirm it from the link we email you (or a person at Oneway accepts it), we take the post down and tell its author how to answer. If we remove yours and you think we were wrong, you can send a counter-notice: unless the person who complained tells us they have gone to court, the post comes back after 14 days. We may end the accounts of people who repeatedly infringe; three posts with a standing notice open a case about the person.

The law: these steps follow the Digital Millennium Copyright Act (17 U.S.C. 512). In plain words: tell us what is yours and where it is, and promise it is true; the poster can answer, and repeat infringers lose their accounts.

11. Messages and email

Covers: Messages, group chats, a Center’s inbox, the Marketplace chat, the email inbox

Messages are between the people in the conversation. New conversations start with messages that disappear after 2 days, and the room's settings decide who can change that. Do not rely on a disappearing message to stay private: anyone who receives one can copy it.

A message to a business goes to whoever it set up to receive it, and the conversation says whether that is an AI assistant, a person or a team.

A Marketplace chat keeps its messages, and warns you when someone asks you to pay ahead.

The email inbox. You can link mail accounts you are allowed to use and read them in Oneway. When you send mail from Oneway, it goes as that account, and you are responsible for it, as you would be in that provider’s own app. If you give a business address to a Center’s inbox, its team can read and reply to that mail until you take it back.

12. Connected accounts

Covers: Settings under Connected accounts, a Center’s connected accounts and Marketing in the OS

You can connect accounts on other platforms, such as Instagram, Facebook, YouTube and Google Business Profile. Before each connection, Oneway lists each permission it asks for and why, and you agree to each one. The platform's own terms and its own consent screen also apply.

When you connect YouTube, Oneway uses YouTube API Services, and by using that connection you agree to be bound by the YouTube Terms of Service . Google’s Privacy Policy covers what Google does with your data.

Oneway posts to a platform only what you pick to post.

You are responsible for following each platform's rules for what you post there. A platform can end or limit a connection, and we are not responsible when it does.

A post can show another platform’s video player. That platform’s terms apply to its player.

Disconnect any time in Settings.

13. Centers and the OS

Covers: a Center’s page in the App, its operating side in the OS, its team and workspace profiles, its Brain

Every organization, business and city can have a Center. A Center has two sides: its page in the App, which people see and follow, and its operating side in the OS, where its team works. The people who run a Center manage it from the OS. The Center is its operators' responsibility: its content, its staff, its customers, its records and its compliance with the law.

A Center keeps its own records about its customers. Oneway stores and handles them for the Center. The Center decides how they are used, must have a lawful basis to hold them, tell its customers about them, and answer their requests.

A Center may list its people by their work names. It must not use a coworker’s workspace profile to find their personal one.

Oneway is software. It is not a gaming operator, does not hold a gaming licence, and does not give legal, tax or compliance advice. A Center is responsible for the reports it files, the records it keeps and the rules that apply to it, including gaming, anti-money-laundering and privacy law.

A Center must not use Oneway to contact, recognise, reward or admit a person it is required to exclude, such as someone on a self-exclusion list.

A Center must treat a recognition suggestion as unconfirmed until a person at the Center has checked it, and must not use one to harass, discriminate against or pursue someone.

If a Center sends email or text messages through Oneway, it is the sender. It must have the recipients' consent where the law requires it, honor opt-outs at once, and follow the CAN-SPAM Act and the Telephone Consumer Protection Act.

Oneway does not provide facial recognition. A Center must not use Oneway to run face recognition on people, and must follow the law, including posting any notice it requires, for anything it does with its own tools.

A Center that offers itself as a safe meetup spot for the Marketplace confirms it is public, staffed and lit.

Two-step sign-in is required in casino, guest, rewards and credential areas. Do not share access.

If you own a Center, hand it over before you delete your account.

14. Data processing for Centers

Covers: a Center’s customer, guest and staff records in the OS

For the records a Center keeps about its customers, staff and guests, the Center decides why and how they are used, and Oneway is its processor. In plain words: they are the Center’s records, and we only handle them for it. As the processor, Oneway will:

use those records only to provide the Service to the Center and on its instructions, which are the Center's settings and its use of the Service, and for no purpose of our own;

keep them confidential, and let only people who need them to run the Service see them;

protect them with reasonable administrative, technical and physical safeguards;

use the service providers named in the Privacy Policy, hold each to the same duties, and name any new one in the Privacy Policy;

help the Center answer a customer's or staff member's request to see, correct or delete a record;

tell the Center without undue delay, and within 72 hours, if we learn of a breach that affects its records, so it can notify the people and the authorities the law requires;

delete or return the records when the Center ends its use of the Service, within 30 days of its request, except where the law requires us to keep them; and

give the Center, on request, the information it needs to show that we meet these duties.

The Center must give its customers and staff the notices the law requires, and must not give us records it has no right to hold.

15. Bookings, tickets, deposits and disputes

Covers: booking on a Center’s page, event tickets, booking and stay deposits, buying from a Center

The Center is the seller. When you book, buy a ticket or pay a deposit, your agreement is with the Center, and it is responsible for what it sells, its prices, its cancellations and its refunds.

You pay on Stripe’s page, to the Center’s own Stripe account, and Stripe’s terms apply to the payment. You do not need a Oneway account to pay.

Deposits. A booking’s deposit is set by the Center’s rule when you book, and a later change to that rule does not change it.

Disputes. If you dispute a payment with your bank, the bank and Stripe decide it with the Center. While a dispute is open, what you bought may be paused, for example a ticket put on hold. Talk to the Center first; most problems are solved faster that way.

16. The Marketplace

Covers: Marketplace listings, Message the seller, the listing chat, safe meetup spots

Who. Selling and messaging a seller are for people 18 and over. Under 18, you can browse.

Your listing must be yours to sell, honest about its condition, and in the right category. A listing shows an approximate area, never your address.

Never sold here: weapons (knives, swords and tasers too), drugs (prescription pills, CBD and delta-8 too), alcohol, tobacco and vapes, adult items, live animals, fireworks, counterfeits and gift cards. We refuse a listing that names them, and you can report one that slips through.

Meet safely. Meet in a busy public place in daylight. The chat suggests safe meetup spots first: Centers that offer themselves as public, staffed and lit.

Paying. Today you pay in person at pickup, after you check the item. Never pay ahead by Zelle, Venmo, Cash App, a deposit or a gift card, and never share a code sent to your phone. Oneway is not a party to the sale and does not handle the money. Paying through Oneway and shipping are not available on the Marketplace yet.

17. Rewards and loyalty programs

Covers: a Center’s rewards program in the OS, your rewards standing

A Center’s rewards program is the Center’s. Its points, tiers and offers are set by the Center under its own rules, and Oneway does not guarantee them.

A Center can link your number in its program to you only on something you have proven, such as your verified email. Your standing moves between businesses only if you turn that on.

Casino offers are for people 21 and over, everywhere.

18. Sign in with Oneway and apps

Covers: Sign in with Oneway on other sites, Popit apps, integrations a Center installs, widgets

This section applies to anyone who builds a site, app or integration on Oneway, including every Sign in with Oneway gateway, any Popit app, and any app a Center installs.

Ask only for what you need, and use only what the person or Center agreed to share. A grant is per person or per Center, and it can be revoked at any time. Stop using the data, and delete what you hold, when it is revoked.

Do not sell the data, use it for advertising, use it to train AI models, or combine it with other data to identify people elsewhere.

Publish a privacy policy that says what you collect from Oneway and why, and keep the data secure.

Do not scrape, and do not reach Oneway data except through the access you were given.

Tell us promptly if the data you received from Oneway is exposed.

We may limit or disable an app that breaks these rules or puts people at risk.

19. AI features and the Brain

Covers: AI features in Create, a Center’s AI assistant in its inbox, your Brain in Me, a Center’s Brain in the OS

Some features use AI to write or suggest text and images. It can be wrong or unsuitable. Nothing is published for you without your choice. You are responsible for what you choose to post or send, for the accuracy of what you publish, and for following each platform's rules for it.

Where an AI answers a message for a Center, the conversation says so.

If you use AI to make an advertisement with an AI-generated person in it, you must disclose that as New York law requires.

As between you and Oneway, you own what an AI feature produces for you, subject to these Terms and to the rights of anyone whose content it may resemble.

Your Brain page is counted from your own activity and does not call an AI model.

A Center’s Brain recommends, and a person at the Center decides. It acts by itself only within what the Center’s owner allowed, and never moves money or acts on a person’s identity alone. The Center is responsible for what its Brain does under its settings.

20. Privacy

The Privacy Policy says what we collect, how we use it and what you control. It is part of these Terms.

21. Our rights

Oneway owns the Service: its software, design, name and marks. You may use it as these Terms allow and for no other purpose. You may not copy or reverse-engineer it except where the law lets you.

22. Third-party services

The Service connects to services we do not run, such as the platforms you connect, mail providers, maps, payments, email and AI providers. Their terms govern your use of them. We do not control them and are not responsible for them.

23. Plans and billing

Covers: Oneway OS, Business OS, selling through Oneway

Oneway is free for people, and Oneway OS is free for any Center.

Business OS is $330 per month for one Center, and Oneway sets it up with you by contact; more than one Business Center is priced by agreement. Any other plan’s price is shown to you before you agree to it. No plan stops your work at a limit it does not show you.

When a Center sells through Oneway, Oneway’s fee is 1% of the sale or less. An order with a fee pays at least 10 cents, never more than the price of what was bought. The Center pays Stripe’s card fees. The fee is refunded in the same share as the sale is refunded, or lost in a dispute.

When you buy from a Center, you do not need an account; the Center is the seller and is responsible for what it sells. You pay on Stripe’s page, to the Center’s own Stripe account, and Stripe’s terms apply to the payment. The Center’s Stripe account is a Standard account: its own, with its own Stripe dashboard.

Nothing is charged today. When billing opens, the price, the billing period, the renewal date and how to cancel are shown to you before you agree, and nothing is charged without your agreement.

Paid plans renew each month until you cancel. You can cancel online at any time, and it takes effect at the end of the period you have paid for. We will tell you before the renewal if a plan renews for a year or longer.

We give 30 days' notice before a price changes. Prices do not include taxes. Fees are not refunded, except where the law requires it.

24. No warranty

THE SERVICE IS PROVIDED "AS IS" AND "AS AVAILABLE", WITHOUT WARRANTIES OF ANY KIND, EXPRESS OR IMPLIED, INCLUDING MERCHANTABILITY, FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE AND NON-INFRINGEMENT. WE DO NOT PROMISE THAT IT WILL BE UNINTERRUPTED, ERROR-FREE OR SECURE, OR THAT CONTENT WILL NOT BE LOST. THIS IS A SELECTIVE SERVER TEST LAUNCH.

In plain words: Oneway is a test launch. We work hard on it, but we cannot promise it will always work, never lose anything, or suit your purpose.

25. Limit of liability

TO THE EXTENT THE LAW ALLOWS, ONEWAY'S TOTAL LIABILITY TO YOU FOR ANY CLAIM ABOUT THE SERVICE OR THESE TERMS IS LIMITED TO THE GREATER OF WHAT YOU PAID US IN THE 12 MONTHS BEFORE THE CLAIM AND $100. WE ARE NOT LIABLE FOR INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL, CONSEQUENTIAL OR PUNITIVE DAMAGES, OR FOR LOST PROFITS OR DATA. NOTHING HERE LIMITS LIABILITY THAT THE LAW DOES NOT ALLOW US TO LIMIT.

In plain words: if something goes wrong, the most we owe you is what you paid us in the last 12 months, or $100 if that is more, unless the law says otherwise.

26. Your responsibility

You will defend and reimburse Oneway against claims, losses and reasonable legal costs that come from your content, your breach of these Terms or your breach of the law. If you use the Service for a Center, this also covers your Center's records and its operators' acts.

In plain words: if someone sues us over something you posted or did, you cover it.

27. Ending

You can stop using Oneway and delete your account at any time, in Settings. Deleting takes 30 days: your profile is hidden at once, and you can change your mind in that time. We may suspend or end your access if you break these Terms, if the law requires it, or if we close the Service. Sections that by their nature should continue, such as what you post, our rights, no warranty, the limit of liability, your responsibility and disputes, continue after that.

28. Governing law and disputes

Law. New York law governs these Terms and any dispute about the Service, without regard to its conflict-of-laws rules, and the Federal Arbitration Act governs the arbitration clause below.

Talk first. Write to us at the address below and give us 30 days to put it right before you start a claim.

Arbitration. If we cannot resolve it, any claim between you and Oneway goes to binding arbitration run by the American Arbitration Association under its rules for consumers or for businesses, whichever applies. It is decided by one arbitrator, on an individual basis, and the arbitrator can give the same relief a court could. We pay the fees beyond what a court filing would cost you.

Not covered. Either of us may bring a claim in small claims court, and either may go to court to stop misuse of intellectual property or of the Service.

No class actions. Claims are brought only on your own behalf, not as a plaintiff or class member in a class or representative action.

Your choice. You can opt out of arbitration and the class waiver by emailing us within 30 days of first accepting these Terms, saying that you opt out. Then the courts of the State of New York, and the federal courts located there, hear the dispute, and you and we consent to them.

In plain words: tell us first. If we still disagree, a single arbitrator decides instead of a court, one person’s claim at a time, unless you opt out by email within 30 days.

29. Notices

We may notify you in the App, by email to the address on your account, or on this page. You may notify us at the address below. You agree to receive notices electronically.

30. Changes

We may change these Terms. We will show a material change in the App at least 14 days before it takes effect, and ask again where the law or a platform requires it. If you keep using the Service after that date, you accept the change. If you do not accept it, delete your account.

Oneway network boosts

Oneway may give an eligible public post labeled network boosts over one to three days. A boosted post's displayed like count includes those boosts; they do not represent individual people and never appear as people in its likes list. We tell the author when a boost is planned. Network boosts do not count toward advertising results, paid placement, business engagement insights or creator earnings. They can stop if the post becomes private, is removed, or the network turns boosts off.

31. The rest

These Terms and the Privacy Policy are the whole agreement between you and Oneway about the Service. If a part cannot be enforced, the rest still applies. If we do not enforce a part right away, we have not given it up. Neither of us is responsible for a delay caused by something beyond its control. No one else has rights under these Terms. You may not transfer your account or these Terms. We may transfer ours if Oneway is merged or sold.

## Data Deletion

Source: https://oneway.center/data-deletion (last changed 2026-11-08)

Our Mission
App
OS
Security
Contact

Sign in

Data Deletion

How to delete what is yours on Oneway, from one post to your whole account: what goes at once, what is kept, for how long, and why. The Privacy Policy is the full account of what we hold.

Contents A post or a photo A comment A connected account A copy of your data Your whole account What is kept, and why For Meta, Threads, Instagram and Facebook

On your profile

A post or a photo

Open the post in the Oneway App

Press Delete , then Delete for good?

It leaves your profile, every feed and every Center it was posted to at once, with its photos and videos.

A photo goes with the post it is in. The files themselves are erased when you delete your account.

Under a post

A comment

Open the post and find your comment

Press Delete beside it

It leaves the conversation at once, and the post's count goes down.

Instagram, Facebook, Threads and the others

A connected account

In the Oneway App, open Settings , then Connected accounts

Press Disconnect beside the account, then press it again

The access the platform gave Oneway is deleted straight away, and nothing more is sent there. Where connecting it verified that account on your profile, the verified mark goes with it.

An account connected for a Center you run is disconnected the same way, in Oneway OS under Settings , then Connected accounts .

Posts already sent stay on the platform, where you can delete them. Posts you imported from it stay on Oneway as your posts, and you delete each one like any other post. Instagram is the exception: disconnecting it deletes every post Oneway brought from Instagram, with its picture. The platform keeps Oneway in its own list of connected apps until you remove it there too.

Before you delete anything

A copy of your data

In the Oneway App, open Settings , then Download your data . Enter your password and press Make my copy . You get one file with your profile, posts, messages, follows, Centers and the links to your photos and videos. It is made in the background, you are told when it is ready, and its download lasts 72 hours. In the same Settings, What Oneway knows about you shows what Oneway understands about you. If you cannot sign in, email hello@oneway.center from the address on your account. We answer within 30 days, and may need to confirm it is you.

Everything, with 30 days to change your mind

Your whole account

In the Oneway App, open Settings , then Delete your account

Enter your password, and the code from your authenticator app if two-step is on

Press Delete your account , then Tap again to delete it in 30 days

If you are the only owner of a Center, hand it to someone else or close it first, in Oneway OS; you are told which one. Your own space is not a Center you run, and it goes with your account.

At once: every session, on every device, and your profile leaves view and search. For 30 days you can change your mind: sign in and press Keep my account .

What is removed: Every session on every device, and every other way in: passkeys, device sign-ins and your widgets’ keys. Your profile, picture, @handle and search listings. Your posts, with their words and pictures, including posts you deleted before. Your comments. Your reactions, reposts and saves. Your follows, blocks and mutes. Your Center memberships and your own space. Sites you signed in to with Oneway. Photos, videos and files you uploaded. What your Brain kept. The accounts you connected, with the access we held for them, and your linked mail accounts with their mail. Your linked identities. Your shared location, your Footsteps and your Waypass. What reached your screen, and what the feed learned from it. Your list of bookings, your Marketplace listings, your work name and title, your settings, your custom feeds and plans, the record of when you were online, and your notifications. Your profile strength score.

After the 30 days it cannot be undone, and nobody can sign in to it again. If you cannot sign in, email us from the address on the account.

After you delete

What is kept, and why

What How long, and why

Your email address, the day you joined and the day you left Kept, with no end date, so no one else can register the address and inherit your history.

Comments and messages you left in other people's conversations Your comments are removed. Messages you sent stay in the other person’s chat, as their copy, shown as from Oneway user with no picture or profile.

A post or a comment you deleted Gone from view at once. Its record stays in our database, so a reply or a share that pointed at it can say it was removed.

What a Center keeps Its own records, its bookings, the pictures uploaded for it and the accounts connected for it stay with the Center: they are its records, not your profile's.

The security log Kept after you delete your account, because it is the record of sign-ins and changes to who can get in. We have not set an end date. We will set one and publish it in the Privacy Policy before the App opens to the public.

Casino compliance records At least five years, as the law requires. They cannot be deleted on request.

Backups A copy of the database is made once a day and kept 14 days, so a copy that still holds your account is gone within 14 days after it is removed.

Legal holds Longer only when the law, a regulator or a legal claim requires it, and only for as long as it does.

We made this page for Meta, Threads, Instagram and Facebook. Hello!

Your deletion request

Where it stands

What Oneway receives from Facebook

When you connect a Facebook Page

The access Facebook gives Oneway: a key for your Facebook account and one for each Page you chose. They are kept encrypted and are never shown back to anyone.

Each Page's name and ID, and, for the Page Oneway posts to, the ID of the Instagram professional account linked to it, if it has one. Instagram can come through this Facebook sign-in, or through its own, below.

If you start an import: the Page's posts, with their photos and videos, copied onto Oneway as posts.

Oneway uses it to send the posts you pick to that Page and its Instagram account, and to copy the Page's posts when you start an import. It never receives your Facebook password, and it does not ask Facebook for your friends or your messages. Threads connects through its own sign-in and gives Oneway its own key, with your Threads account's ID and username.

What Oneway receives from Instagram

When you connect Instagram with its own sign-in

The access Instagram gives Oneway, kept encrypted and never shown back to anyone.

Your Instagram account's ID, username, name and account type (Business or Creator).

When you press Import, or while Bring my new posts is on (Oneway then reads your newest posts every 15 minutes): each post's caption, its link and a copy of its picture, kept as a Oneway post that plays in Instagram's own player, marked From Instagram.

Oneway posts to Instagram only what you pick on a post. It never receives your Instagram password, your messages or your followers.

On Instagram

Remove Oneway from your Instagram account

In Instagram, open Settings , then Website permissions

Open Apps and websites , then Active

Press Remove beside Oneway

Meta tells Oneway, and Oneway deletes the access it held and every post it brought from that Instagram account, with its picture.

On Facebook

Remove Oneway from your Facebook account

On Facebook, open Settings & privacy , then Settings

Open Apps and websites ( facebook.com/settings?tab=applications )

Find Oneway Services and press Remove

Facebook ends the access it gave Oneway: Oneway can no longer post to your Pages or read them.

What Oneway already received stays with Oneway until you delete it, below.

On Oneway

Delete what Oneway received from Facebook

In the Oneway App, open Settings , then Connected accounts . For a Center, open Oneway OS, then Settings , then Connected accounts

Press Disconnect beside Facebook, then press it again. Do the same beside Instagram

Oneway deletes the access it held for them straight away, with each Page's name and ID, and nothing more is sent to them.

Posts you imported from Facebook are Oneway posts: delete each one like any other post. Posts brought from Instagram are deleted when you disconnect Instagram, with their pictures.

Deleting your Oneway account deletes the Facebook and Instagram connections on your profile too, and every post brought from Instagram. Or email williamrau78@gmail.com from the address on your Oneway account with the name of the Facebook Page, and we delete what Oneway received from Facebook for it. We answer within 30 days, and may need to confirm it is you.

Contact

To have anything else removed, email us. We answer within 30 days.

williamrau78@gmail.com

Centers

A place for just about anything.

Your favorite restaurant, a neighborhood across the world, or a community built around something you love. Each can have its own Center on Oneway.

Centers bring together posts, photos, information, conversations, and things to do. Explore a place’s history, see what people are sharing, or create a community of your own.

Open Discovery → Explore Oneway OS →

What a Center can be

As simple or as large as its purpose.

An Information Center
A page about a place, started by whoever knows it. People add a line, a photo and a link.

A claimed Center
An organization takes ownership of the page that is already there.

A community
Posts, events and conversation for what people love, tied to a place or to none.

A business
Its menu, products, events and bookings, and the OS behind them.

Its Canvas
Arrange its layout, its pages and its interactive elements.

Its website
Build one from the same Center, on a domain of its own.

## Waypass

Source: https://oneway.center/waypass (last changed 2026-11-08)

Our Mission App OS Security Contact

Sign in

Waypass

You never know who you’ll cross paths with.

You might visit the same coffee shop, attend the same events, or pass someone regularly without ever meeting.

Waypass helps people who opt in discover others whose paths have crossed through shared places. Explore their Profiles and choose whether to connect, without making your live location public.

Join Oneway → Open Discovery →

How it works

Your choice, at every step.

Off until you turn it on
Nobody is in Waypass who did not choose to be.

Between people who both turn it on
You see who you passed only if they take part too.

Really there, at the same moment
Two phones with Oneway open, within about 150 metres of each other, swap cards. A few minutes later you are both told at once. Being in the same part of town hours apart is not a pass.

Places, not a live dot
It shows that paths crossed at a public place. It does not put you on a live map.

You decide what happens next
Look at their Profile, connect, or leave it.

Remove it
Take someone you passed off your list.

18 and over
A teen account’s Waypass stays off.

Discovery
Security
Safety

Someone you haven’t met yet.

Cross Projection

Your world, connected across the web.

Oneway works alongside the accounts, websites, and services you already use.

A venue can create an event, upload its artwork, and prepare it for its Center, website, social media accounts, and digital displays. Connected information can be updated, checked for differences, and published to supported destinations.

Businesses keep their websites, customer accounts, and existing tools while connecting more of the experience.

Cross Projection comes with Oneway OS, which is coming soon.

Business OS early access Explore Oneway OS →

One event, start to finish

More than reposting.

One record
Your Center holds the event; each place it appears reads from that.

Each destination’s own shape
The artwork and words are prepared for where they will appear.

Approvals
Nothing goes out until a person approves it.

Differences checked
When a connected source says something different, you are told, with both answers. You decide.

Supported destinations
It publishes where a connection is supported. It is not two-way sync with everything.

The visitor’s way
Someone finding the event books through the venue’s own website or its chosen service.

About

Oneway Technologies

Oneway Technologies LLC is the New York company developing Oneway.

Oneway is the platform: an emerging social network connecting people, places, communities, and more of the web. Oneway Technologies is the company that makes it.

Making entertainment, connection, and the Internet better for all sides.

Our Mission Contact

What the company makes

One ecosystem, for people and for the places around them.

The Oneway App
The social network: Home, Discovery, Create, Messages and your Profile.

Oneway OS
Where a Center is run: its page, website, posts, events and community.

Business OS
Systems, team tools and the Brain, added to a Center.

Developer OS
For building applications, Systems and integrations on Oneway. Coming soon.

Our Mission

The problem it works on
Not everything has to start on Oneway. Someone can start with a Google search, an external website, another social platform, a friend’s message, or a physical place. Oneway gives those experiences somewhere to continue, without asking people or businesses to abandon the platforms they already use.

Where it is now
Our first launch is New York City. What changes is written on the changelog, each update dated.

## What Oneway's words mean

Source: https://oneway.center/learn (last changed 2026-11-08)

Our Mission App OS Security Contact

Sign in

Learn

What Oneway's words mean.

Oneway has its own words for its parts. Here is what each one means, as the platform is built today.

Oneway is in its Closed Selective Server Beta.

Profile

A Profile is a person's one identity on Oneway, with an @name, the same in the App and in Oneway OS. You choose how it looks and what it shows, and you can make it private.

Explore the App

Guest

A guest is anyone using Oneway without an account; in the App, “Look around first” starts as one. A guest can explore the map and Discovery, and like a post, which is kept on their device and counts once they sign in. Where a Center lets anyone ask, a guest can ask it a question and get its answer by email, or leave a phone number for the Center to call back. Commenting, reposting and saving need an account.

Without an account

Center

A Center is what a place, a community or a business is on Oneway: one object with two sides. Its public side is what anyone sees in the App, and its operating side is Oneway OS, where its team runs it. Founding a Center makes both sides at once.

What a Center is

Canvas

A canvas is a page its owner arranges. Every Center is one: its team places Popits on it in Oneway OS, moves and sizes them, and a visitor sees it as it was laid out, in fewer columns on a phone. Your Home in the App is a canvas of your own.

Popit

A Popit is one live piece of a canvas, drawn from one thing its owner keeps: its latest posts, what is coming up, its links or its website. When that thing changes, every Popit that shows it changes with it.

Popits in Oneway OS

Systems

Systems are the tools a kind of place runs on, such as a hotel's operations, a restaurant's floor or a community's membership, added to a Center from the System Store. Each one works from the same Center, and which ones a Center can add depends on its OS.

The System Store

Oneway OS

Oneway OS is the operating side of a Center, where its team builds and runs it. Its base layer is free: the Center's page and identity, its posts, events, announcements, groups, Popits and community. Business OS is built on top of it, and so is Developer OS.

Explore Oneway OS

Business OS

Business OS is what a business adds to its Center: a team with roles and departments, bookings, the Systems of its industry, the Brain, Cross Projection and Lightbulb LED.

Explore Business OS Buy Business OS today

Developer OS

Developer OS is for building on Oneway: sites where people sign in with Oneway, Systems built on the same contract as Oneway's own, and integrations that report into a Center. It is free to start, and coming soon.

Explore Developer OS

The Brain

The Brain is a Center's understanding of itself, read from the Center's own records: what needs a person, what it knows apart from what it has only found, and the changes it recommends. It does something on its own only when the Center's owner allows it, and only what can be put back. It comes with Business OS.

Compatibility and the Brain

Cross Projection

Cross Projection keeps one record of a Center behind every place it appears: the App, the Center's page and its own website. When a connected source shows something different, such as new hours, a person approves the change before the record moves, and everything that reads the record follows. It comes with Business OS.

Compatibility and integration

Lightbulb (Create)

Lightbulb, labelled Create in the App, is where you make something: a post, a document, a note, a page to write or draw on, or a place for the map. What you make goes where it belongs, a post to a feed and a document to your Workspace. A Center's team makes things as the Center with Lightbulb LED, which comes with Business OS.

Lightbulb in the App

Discovery

Discovery is where you find places, events, people and communities on Oneway, starting from a map. Signed out, it shows the places anyone can walk into; signed in, it starts from the Centers you follow and the communities you join.

Discovery in the App

Teen mode and parent supervision

Teen mode is how the App runs for anyone 13 to 17: stricter from the first day about who can message them, who sees their posts and what reaches their phone at night. Supervision is a parent the teen invites, who can only make it stricter.

Teen accounts Supervision

Is a word missing, or unclear?
Ask us

Oneway, in plain words.

What is Oneway?
Oneway is a social network and a business platform in one. Every person has one profile, and every community, place and business has a Center.

Does Oneway have a feed like Instagram?
Yes. Home has a For You feed ranked to what you like and a Following feed of only the people and places you follow, with photo and video posts, and stories at the top that last 24 hours. You can also make custom feeds from people, places and words, newest first or top this week, pin them as tabs on Home, and share a public one for anyone to pin.

How do people find places on Oneway?
Through Discovery: a map and search of the people, places and Centers near you. A Center can start as an information page, its facts checked by a person, and its owner claims it when they join.

What is a Center?
A Center is the home of a place, a community or a business on Oneway. At its simplest it is an information page; it can also be a social profile, a website on its own domain, a storefront and the workspace its team runs it from.

What is Oneway OS?
Oneway OS is where a Center is run: its page and website, posts, events and community, free. Business OS adds bookings, staff and the Systems of its industry.

Who controls my data?
You choose what your profile shows, and your work for a Center stays apart from your personal activity. You can delete your data and your account; if you own a Center, you hand it over first.

## Community Guidelines

Source: https://oneway.center/community-guidelines (last changed 2026-11-08)

Our Mission App OS Security Contact

Sign in

Guidelines

Community Guidelines

The rules for everyone on Oneway, what happens to an account or a Center that breaks them, and how to ask us to look at a decision again.

They apply everywhere on Oneway: profiles, posts, comments, messages and Centers. They sit beside the Terms of Service . Updated 17 October 2026.

Not allowed

What is not allowed on Oneway.

None of these, anywhere on Oneway, in public or in private.

Harassment
Do not harass, bully or stalk anyone, or keep contacting someone who has made it clear they do not want you to.

Hate
Do not attack or demean people for their race, ethnicity, national origin, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, disability or serious illness.

Threats and violence
Do not threaten to hurt anyone, push someone to hurt themselves, or promote violence or terrorism.

Sexual content involving minors
Never post, share or ask for sexual content involving anyone under 18, or anything that sexualizes a child, exploits one or puts one in danger. There are no exceptions.

Intimate images without consent
Do not share, or threaten to share, a nude or sexual image or video of someone without their consent, including one that is faked or edited to look real.

Impersonation
Do not pretend to be another person, a business, an organization or Oneway.

Spam and scams
Do not spam people, phish for their passwords or money, or run a scam. Do not fake reviews, or buy followers, likes or comments.

Illegal goods and services
Do not sell, buy, trade or arrange anything illegal, such as illegal drugs, stolen goods, or weapons sold outside the law.

Private information
Do not share someone's private information without their consent: their home address, phone number, documents or where they are. Do not use a place's guest list, location sharing or StreetPass to find or follow someone.

What happens

What Oneway does when a rule is broken.

A person decides every report. A machine can raise a report for a person to look at, but it never decides one.

Reports
However often one person reports the same thing, it counts once. How to report someone, or block or mute them, is on Safety .

The word check
A post written in the App is checked for hateful, threatening and sexual words, some disguised spellings included. What it finds waits for a person, and the check hides nothing by itself.

A Center's own space
A Center's team can remove comments left on its posts, and you can remove comments left on posts on your own profile. A complaint about a Center is decided by Oneway, never by that Center.

Community notes
Where readers have added context to a post, it shows under the post, and anyone signed in, other than its writer, can rate it helpful or not helpful. How it shows comes from those ratings, and no note is ever labelled as verified.

Removal
Oneway can take a Center that breaks these rules out of search, the map and everywhere else it is shown, its posts with it.

Restricting an account
Oneway can restrict an account that breaks these rules, for a set time or until it is lifted. Every session it has ends at once, it cannot sign in, and the person is told the reason when they try.

Appeals

Ask for a decision to be looked at again.

If you think a decision about you is wrong, you can appeal it.

How to appeal
Write to us from the contact page : which decision it was, and why you think it is wrong.

Who can appeal
Only the person a decision was about, never the person who made the report.

What follows
When an appeal overturns a decision, a restriction that rested on it is lifted and the person is told. Every decision is recorded with who made it.

Look out for each other.
Safety on Oneway Terms of Service

## Safety

Source: https://oneway.center/safety (last changed 2026-11-08)

Our Mission App OS Security Contact

Sign in

Safety

Safety on Oneway

The controls you have, the protections teen accounts start with, how a parent can supervise, and how to reach us when something is wrong.

The rules everyone keeps to, and what happens when someone does not, are in the Community Guidelines . How the platform itself is protected is on Security . Updated 17 October 2026.

Block, mute, report

Stop anyone reaching you.

On a person's profile, press More beside Follow and Message. In a chat with one person, open Chat settings, then Privacy and safety.

Block
They can no longer message you, mention you or see your posts. Follows between you end, what they already sent leaves your notifications, and they are not told. Undo it in Settings, under Blocked accounts; follows do not come back on their own.

Mute
Their posts stop reaching your feed, and nothing else changes; they are not told. To undo it, find them in Settings, under Muted accounts.

Report
Choose what is wrong: spam, harassment, hate, violence, nudity, self harm, misinformation, impersonation, intellectual property, illegal, or other. Nobody is told who reported it.

Anything else
To report a post, a comment, a message or a Center, tell us through the contact page and say where it is on Oneway.

Teen accounts

Teen accounts start protected.

Oneway asks your birthday when you join the App, and your age decides which of these apply. No one under 13 can join.

Private to start
A teen's profile starts private.

Messages
Only people a teen follows can message them, whatever their other settings say.

Bedtime
Between 10 PM and 7 AM their time, no push notification goes to their phone; what comes in waits in their list in the App. No more than three push notifications are sent in a day.

Daily limit
After 60 minutes in a day, the App says so and offers to keep going. It never cuts them off. Their time each day and over the week is in Settings, under Supervision.

13 to 15
Oneway does not suggest their posts to strangers, and a parent must approve before their profile is open to everyone.

Not in search
No one under 18 is listed in Google or any other search engine.

Your birthday
It is never shown to anyone else. How it is kept, and the rest of what applies to someone under 18, is in the Privacy Policy .

Supervision

A parent can supervise.

Only the teen can start it, and it ends on its own when they turn 18.

Starting it
The teen invites a parent in Settings, under For families, Supervision. The parent needs a Oneway account of their own, with a birthday showing they are 18 or over, and has 7 days to accept. A teen can have two parents supervising.

Limits, only stricter
A parent can make bedtime longer and the day shorter, never the other way: bedtime can start as early as 6 PM and end as late as 10 AM, and a day can be as short as 15 minutes.

Approvals
A teen's ask to open their profile goes to the parent, who decides, and the teen is told either way.

What a parent sees
The protections in force, what the teen has asked for, and who the teen talks to, by name. Never what they say, never a group's name, and never the teen's birthday.

Ending it
Either of them can end it at any time, and the other is told. When no parent is left, the stricter limits end with it.

Privacy

Choose who sees you and who reaches you.

Each one is in the App's Settings: look under Privacy, or under Messages.

Private profile
Only friends, people you follow who follow you back, see what you post.

Who can message you
Friends, people from your Centers and people you have crossed paths with each have a switch, and Anyone stays off until you choose it. Unless you change it, a first message from someone new waits in Message requests.

Comments
Let anyone comment, or only friends and people from your Centers.

Search engines
Keep your profile and public posts out of Google and other search engines. A link someone shares still opens.

Online and typing
Hide when you are online, and when you are typing.

Lists and counts
Hide who follows you and who you follow. Hide the counts of reactions and replies on your posts, or on everything you see.

Location
Share where you are with nobody, people you name, followers, friends, your Centers or everyone, exactly or approximately. Turning it off deletes it.

Let places recognise you
Turn it off and no place is offered a match with you. How a match is made, and what a place sees once you are linked, is in the Privacy Policy .

Images and child safety

Intimate images and child safety.

If an intimate image is shared without consent, or anything sexualizes a child, report it as soon as you see it. Do not share it further, and do not send it to us.

In the App
Open the profile of whoever shared it, press More, then Report, and choose nudity or illegal.

Anywhere else
Use the contact page and give a link to where it is, or the account's name.

If someone threatens you
If someone says they will share an image of you unless you pay or send more, you do not have to do either. Report them first, then block them.

Help outside Oneway
NCMEC's CyberTipline takes reports of child sexual exploitation. Take It Down helps with images taken before you were 18, and StopNCII.org helps adults. They are run by others, not by Oneway, and work with the platforms that take part in them.
If someone is in danger now, call 911. If you are thinking about hurting yourself, call or text 988 in the United States.

Your data

Delete what is yours.

Delete a post from the post itself, or your whole account in Settings, under Delete your account. What goes at once and what stays, with the reasons, is on the Data Deletion page.

Data Deletion

Something wrong? Tell us.
Contact

Discovery

The places and people around you.

A map and a feed of what is near, in the Oneway App.

What it does

Find it, open it, add it.

Map and Explore

Place cards

Add a place

Improve this place

Waypass
Who you passed and where, between people who both turn it on.

Saved
Save places into lists, private until you share them.

Contribute
What you added and improved, and what is missing near you.

Controls on the map

## Accessibility

Source: https://oneway.center/accessibility (last changed 2026-11-08)

Our Mission App OS Security Contact

Sign in

Accessibility

Oneway should work for everyone who uses it.

We aim to meet the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 at level AA, on this site and in the App. It is an aim we are working toward, not a certification.

Today

What the site and the App do now.

Keyboard

Every link, button and field on this site shows a ring when you reach it with the keyboard. The App draws its own ring on its controls, from the dock to the rows of Settings.

Motion

When your device asks for reduced motion, this site's sky holds still and its sections appear without rising into place. The App stops moving too: on its Home screen, every animation stops.

The App also has its own switch, in Settings, then Accessibility. Reduce motion turns off the App's animations without changing what you can do, on every device you sign in on.

Contrast

We measure contrast on the rendered page, not only in the code. On Our Mission, Support, this page and the legal pages, every word stands at least 4.8 to 1 against what is behind it, in light and in dark, where level AA asks for 4.5 to 1.

In the App, Higher contrast makes its quieter words and its edges stronger.

Text size

No page on this site or in the App turns off zooming, so you can enlarge any of it with your browser or a pinch. In the App, Larger text enlarges what you read.

Pictures

Every picture on this site has a text alternative, or is marked as decoration so a screen reader passes over it.

Not yet

Where we know we fall short.

Descriptions for your photos

You cannot yet write a description for a photo you post. Until you can, a screen reader hears each one by its place in the post, such as Photo 1.

Some small marks

A few small marks on the landing and the OS page, such as the initials in sample profile pictures and the faint arrows between steps, measure below the contrast level AA asks for.

Arranging a Center's canvas

In Oneway OS, a Center's Popits are moved and sized by holding and dragging them. There is no keyboard way to arrange them yet.

An outside audit

Everything here comes from our own checks. No outside auditor has tested Oneway against WCAG 2.2.

Report a barrier

Tell us what stopped you.

On the contact page, name the page or screen, what you were trying to do, and what you use to get around, such as a screen reader, a keyboard or zoom, so we can fix it.

Report a barrier

This page was last reviewed on 17 October 2026.

## Security

Source: https://oneway.center/security (last changed 2026-11-08)

Our Mission
App
OS
Security
Contact

Sign in

Security

Last updated: October 26, 2026

Our promises

Oneway is new, so here is what you can count on, and where this page shows how.

We never see your password. It is stored scrambled one way, so it cannot be read back. How

Two-step verification is there for every account, with codes from an authenticator app, never by text message. How

Our staff see only your email address and username, unless something is reported or flagged, and every look is logged. How

One business on Oneway can never reach another’s data, and an automated test checks it for every endpoint. How

Secrets are write-only. Passwords for the systems you or a business connect are locked away, and no screen or endpoint shows them back. How

You stay in control of who can reach you and where you are signed in, in Settings. How

A real person answers, and you can report a problem or a vulnerability. How

We claim no certification we do not hold, and we mark what is not built yet. How

What changed

The page is rewritten in plain English, and each section names the features it covers.

New: sign-in limits , what Oneway’s staff can see , moderation, account standing and Shield , and the child-safety check on uploads .

New: linked mail sign-ins are sealed in the same vault as other secrets.

New: our promises , each linked to the part that shows how, and what you control , by its name in Settings.

New: how to reach a person and report a problem or a vulnerability .

One standard for the whole ecosystem. The same protections cover every part of Oneway: your account, profile and messages in the Oneway App; every community’s and business’s Center; the operating side of every Center in Oneway OS, Business OS and Developer OS; every System a Center runs, from a restaurant’s floor and a hotel’s rooms to a venue, a shop and a casino resort; every website a Center wears; and every integration and app built on the platform. A neighborhood group and a casino’s operating floor sit on the same platform, so we hold them to the same bar: the one set by the most regulated industry we serve.

What this page is. Oneway is in a selective server test launch and is not yet running as a public service. This page describes the security built into the platform today, each part exactly as it works. Nothing here claims a certification we do not hold. For how we handle personal information, read the Privacy Policy ; for blocking, reporting and the protections teen accounts start with, read Safety .

Contents Signing in and sessions Between people and between Centers What Oneway’s staff can see Encryption and secrets Integrations and apps Outbound requests In the browser Files and photos Moderation, account standing and Shield The security log What you control Talk to a person, report a problem The standard we hold ourselves to

Signing in and sessions

Covers: sign-up, sign-in, Settings (password, two-step sign-in, sessions), the OS

Passwords are stored as bcrypt hashes (work factor 12), each with its own salt. A hash can check a password but cannot be turned back into it. A password is never stored, logged or returned in plain text.

Two-step sign-in uses six-digit codes from any standard authenticator app (TOTP, RFC 6238). Codes are checked in constant time, so timing gives nothing away, and recovery codes are stored only as hashes. We do not send codes by text message, because SIM swapping defeats them.

Two-step sign-in is available on every account and required where the stakes are highest: the whole operating side of a casino’s Center asks for it by default.

Sessions are kept on our servers. Your browser holds only a random token, in a __Host- cookie marked Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite=Lax. In plain words: it is sent only over HTTPS, only to Oneway, no script on a page can read it, and other sites cannot make your browser use it for a change. Signing out ends the session on the server, not only in the browser.

Changing your password ends every other session on the account at once.

Signing in reveals no account. Signing in or resetting a password while signed out gives the same answer whether or not an address has an account.

Sign-in limits. Failed sign-ins are counted two ways. From one network address: by default 12 in five minutes, then sign-in from there waits until the five minutes pass. For one account, from any network: by default 10 in 15 minutes, then that account’s sign-in waits. The answer is the same whether or not the account exists, and a successful sign-in clears the account’s count.

Rate limits on every endpoint , per session and per network address, so one person’s traffic never uses up another’s. Over the limit, a request is answered with 429 and a Retry-After, and nothing behind the endpoint runs.

Between people and between Centers

Covers: a Center’s operating side in the OS, its roles, every Center endpoint

Authority comes from the relationship, never from the request. What a person may see or do is decided by their real standing with a Center (owner, admin, staff or member) and by what each person has chosen to share, never by an identifier the caller supplies.

One Center can never reach another's operating side. An automated test reads every Center endpoint from the application's own route list and calls each one as the owner of a different Center. A new endpoint is tested the day it is added.

Every change requires a signed-in person. An automated test calls every endpoint that changes anything while signed out; none succeeds, except the few a signed-out person needs, such as signing in and resetting a password.

Roles each Center defines for itself. Beyond owner, admin and staff, a Center can name its own roles. A role can only narrow what a member of staff may see and do, and every role change is written to the security log.

Workspace profiles stay apart. A person’s work name is shown with no @handle to anyone who is not a coworker, so it cannot be joined to their personal profile.

What Oneway’s staff can see

Covers: Oneway’s admin system

The list of accounts shows only each account’s email address and username, beside Oneway’s own notes on it (restricted, reported, its standing).

More opens only for an account that was reported or flagged, and only what the case needs: the reported item and why, the account’s age and recent counts. Never a private message beyond the one reported, never who reported, never an address it signed in from.

Every view and every search is written to the security log first. A view that cannot be logged is not shown.

Only Oneway’s owner, and staff the owner gives this permission, can use it. Restricting an account asks for a reason, and for the staff member’s own password and two-step code, and an admin can never restrict the owner or another staff member from there.

Child-safety records are read only by a named person who holds that one permission, and never through the platform’s key.

Encryption and secrets

Covers: a Center’s integrations, connected accounts, linked mail accounts, two-step sign-in, a casino’s ID records

Every Center has its own secrets vault. Credentials a Center uses to connect its own systems are encrypted with AES-256-GCM under a data key that belongs to that Center alone.

A person’s secrets have their own vault too, such as the sign-in of each mail account they link. It is never shown back.

Envelope encryption. Each vault’s data key is itself encrypted under a master key that is never stored in the database.

Every encrypted value is bound to its place. Each one is sealed together with its owner and its name (authenticated encryption, AEAD). A value copied to another Center, or renamed, fails to open, and any changed byte fails the check.

Secrets are write-only. No endpoint returns a secret, not even to its owner. Operators see a secret’s name, who set it, when, and when an integration last used it. The value reaches only the server code that calls that provider.

Keys are 256-bit values from the operating system’s secure random generator, with a fresh nonce for every encryption.

Key rotation without exposure. Rotating the master key re-wraps each data key. No secret is decrypted to do it.

Crypto-shredding. Removing a Center’s vault destroys its data key, and from that moment the platform can no longer open any secret it held. Encrypted database backups made before the removal still hold the old key until they age out, within 14 days.

Personal secrets, such as a two-step seed, are sealed under a key made for that one purpose and bound to the person they belong to.

In transit: HTTPS everywhere, with HTTP Strict Transport Security for one year across every subdomain.

Integrations and apps

Covers: Connected accounts, a Center’s integrations and feeds, Popit apps, widgets

A business connects its own systems. A provider cannot sign itself in to a Center. Each Center sets up its own integrations, with credentials only it holds, kept in its own vault.

Every connection asks first. Before another platform’s sign-in screen, Oneway lists each permission and why, and the server refuses to connect until each one is agreed.

Every feed has its own key, shown once when it is issued and stored only as a SHA-256 hash. Issuing a new key disables the old one at once.

Signed webhooks. Messages from a connected vendor are checked by their HMAC-SHA256 signature, in constant time, before anything is read, and a signed message is refused once it is too old to be fresh.

Apps built on Oneway , including Popit apps, run on their own sandbox host, under their own content security policy, with only the permissions a person allowed.

Widgets use a token made for one device that can only read its owner’s Home. It is stored as a hash, signs nobody in, and ends with the session that made it.

Outbound requests

Covers: integrations, linked mail accounts, any fetch Oneway’s servers make

Server-side request forgery is when a server is tricked into fetching an address that points back inside its own network. It is how a vendor’s server becomes a way into its customers’ networks. Every request an integration makes goes through one guarded fetcher:

HTTPS only, to the hosts each integration is allowed to reach.

Public internet addresses only. Addresses inside a network (private, loopback, link-local, carrier-grade NAT and reserved ranges), cloud metadata endpoints, and their IPv6 and IPv4-mapped forms are all refused. Mail connections are checked the same way.

The name is looked up once, and the connection is made to exactly the address that was checked. So a name that changes its answer after the check (DNS rebinding) cannot send the request somewhere else.

TLS is verified against the host name, and every redirect is checked again from the start.

Every request is bounded in size and time, and no proxy is taken from the environment.

In the browser

Covers: every Oneway page

X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff : a response is never read as a type other than the one it declares.

frame-ancestors 'self' : no other site can frame Oneway’s pages to trick you into clicking.

Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin : no path or query string leaks to another site.

A Permissions-Policy that allows location, the camera and the microphone only to Oneway’s own pages, each only when you allow it, and shuts Bluetooth, USB, serial ports, HID devices and payment.

Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin , and Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: same-site on data, so another site cannot embed Oneway’s data.

A video player from another platform runs in a sandboxed frame and is sent no referrer.

Files and photos

Covers: every upload: posts, messages, profile and Center pictures, listings, stickers

A file is identified by its bytes (its magic number), never by its name or its declared type. Anything unrecognized is refused.

Sizes are capped before anything is decoded.

Photos are stored without where they were taken or by what. GPS position, device and capture data are removed before storage, without changing a pixel, and the orientation is kept.

Content-addressed storage. Every file is stored under its owner and a SHA-256 digest of its contents. An upload cannot choose its path, climb out of its folder or overwrite anyone else’s file.

The child-safety check is not running yet. Matching photos and videos against lists of known child sexual abuse material needs approval from the service that keeps those lists, which Oneway does not have yet. When it runs, every photo and video passes one writer that checks it before it is stored; if the service cannot answer, the upload is refused, never stored unchecked; and a match is kept locked as evidence that no page serves, the account is held, and a person at Oneway reports it to NCMEC.

Moderation, account standing and Shield

Covers: everything people write, Report, Oneway’s admin system, a Center’s own Shield

Every word is read before it shows , in posts, comments, bios, listings, canvas text and messages, whatever spelling hides it: look-alike letters, numbers for letters, stretched or spaced letters, emoji standing in for words, and masks such as f*ck. It matches whole words, so an ordinary word that contains a short bad one is never caught. It runs on our own servers, with no outside service.

Clear harm is refused, and words that could be harm hold a post for a person to review. Each answer says what to change, and any refusal or hold can be taken to a person.

One standing for each account: normal, watched, held or locked, read once on every write. Three refusals in an hour put an account under watch, and eight hold it. Every move has a reason and an end, is written to the security log, and can be lifted or extended from Oneway’s admin system.

Shield is a set of stricter rules for a raid, each its own switch with a reason and an end, all off with one press: posts and links from new accounts wait for a person, and so do posts from an account whose email is not confirmed. A Center’s managers have their own Shield for its pages and comments. Every change is logged.

Reports are reviewed by people. A case shows the reported item and why, never who reported.

The security log

Covers: Settings (your security page), a Center’s security log in the OS, Oneway’s admin system

A tamper-evident security log records sign-ins, refused sign-ins, changes to how an account is protected, birthday changes, changes to roles and access, and every view in Oneway’s admin system. Each entry is chained to the one before it with an HMAC, so an altered or removed entry shows exactly where. It never records a password, a code, a token or a credential’s value.

Dependencies are pinned to exact versions with cryptographic hashes, on a supported runtime.

What you control

Covers: Settings in the App, by the names it uses

In Settings What it does

Password Change your password. Every other session ends at once.

Two-step verification Turn on codes from an authenticator app, and keep your recovery codes.

Where you are signed in See each session, when it was last used and the browser it came from, and end any of them.

Connected accounts See which other platforms are connected, and disconnect any. The stored access is deleted at once.

Sites you signed in to Take back any site that uses Sign in with Oneway.

Who can message you, Message requests, Blocked accounts Decide who can reach you, let new people wait in requests, and block anyone.

Location sharing Off until you turn it on. Choose who sees it, how exact, and for how long.

Download your data, Delete your account Get a copy of what Oneway holds about you, or delete your account.

The Privacy Policy lists every control, feature by feature.

Talk to a person, report a problem

Covers: everything on this page

Write to hello@oneway.center . A person at Oneway reads and answers.

Think someone else is in your account? Change your password (every other session ends at once), check Where you are signed in, and write to us.

Something wrong on Oneway? Press Report on the post, comment, person, Center or listing. A person reviews every report.

Vulnerability reports are welcome at hello@oneway.center ; our security.txt (RFC 9116) says where to send them. We read every report. Give us a reasonable time to fix it, and do not read, change or keep other people’s data to prove it. We will not take action against good-faith research that follows the Terms .

The standard we hold ourselves to

The bar named at the top of this page, the one the most regulated industry we serve sets for its vendors, is the standard we are building toward: OWASP ASVS Level 3 (the strictest level of a public checklist for web application security) for every endpoint, mapped to a recognized control framework (CIS Controls, ISO/IEC 27001 or NIST SP 800-53), and GLI-GSF-3, the gaming industry’s information security audit for vendors. A SOC 2 Type II report and independent penetration testing are part of that program. This page will say when each is complete, and never before.
